speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by asking: have you noticed bleeding from other sites like gums or nose, or does it happen after minor bumps? Also, when was your last menstrual period, if applicable?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the family history of joint swelling and bleeding in an uncle strongly suggests a hereditary bleeding disorder. Have you ever experienced spontaneous bleeding into your joints or muscles, and do you take any medications like aspirin or ibuprofen? REQUEST TEST: PT/INR, aPTT, Platelet Count, Fibrinogen.

text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Gastroenteritis is incorrect based on the clinical presentation of hemarthrosis and family history; your diagnosis should be Hemophilia A or B. Given the family history of joint swelling in an uncle and the patient's post-extraction bleeding with easy bruising, this is a classic presentation of an X-linked coagulation factor deficiency.
